plan: [ This mechanism is effectively a second-price auction: highest bid wins and pays the second-highest bid (the clock hits the runner-up’s exit). In such auctions, bidding your true private value is a weakly dominant strategy. Shading below risks losing profitable wins without lowering the price you’d pay when you would win anyway. Ties are broken randomly; if tied at 25, expected profit is zero, which is not improved by shading. With 0.1 increments, bid exactly my value. ]

[ The ascending-clock with automatic exit at sealed bids makes the price equal to the second-highest bid. This is effectively a second-price auction. With independent private values, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Overbidding risks paying above value; underbidding risks losing positive-surplus wins. No history to use in round 1 of 1. Bid = 17. ]

[ This two-stage format with automatic dropout at your sealed bid implements a second-price auction among three bidders. With independent private values and risk neutrality, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Overbidding may lead to winning at a price above value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Therefore, bid 39 to win whenever competitors’ highest bid is below 39 and pay the second-highest bid. Ties at 39 are resolved randomly; expected profit is value minus the second-highest bid when winning. ]
